      5 out of 5 stars
      Hell Of A Beast!💚🔥
      I've been continuously using this as my primary device for almost 15 days, with 2 sims inserted. 🤳🏻 Design:- It's a complete personal preference. For me, it's a really unique and professional looking phone. The in-hand feel is even better than that of S22 Ultra and iPhone 13/14 Pro Max because of its Curved screen and Curved sides. 📱Display:- Hands down! This has to be one of the best displays available there in the market. The display is a WQHD, Fluid Amoled LTPO 2.0 Panel with a refresh rate of 120Hz. The peak brightness can go upto 1300 nits, which is more than enough for an average user. Lastly, the display is a “Flagship” display. 🧑🏻‍💻 Performance:- This device comes with Snapdragon 8 Gen1, 12/256 GB, UFS 3.1 Storage solution. Talking about benchmark scores, this device scores a bit less than the Ultra Flagships out there, but that won't be a problem in the day to day usage. This phone feels so smooth, optimised and fast. 💽 Software:- If you've pastly used Oxygen OS 8, 9,10,11, you'll feel a bit different, as the OS has lost its, stock Android appearance. But still, Oxygen OS is the cleanest, when it comes to bloatware, compared to others. It feels so fresh, smooth, optimised and fast, a complete Flagship experience. 🔋 Battery:- The battery experience is quite good. For me, it's giving a Screen On Time (SOT) of around 5-6, even 7 hours sometimes. And the charging is one of the best, with 80W fast charging. And the charger is included inside the box.😅 📸 Camera:- This device comes with a (48MP Wide, 50MP Ultrawide, 8MP Telephoto). The picture comes with a really natural colour output and video also comes with great stabilization and colour output. The only problem is that the Telephoto and Ultrawide can't record in 4K 60Fps. It might be fixed with future updates. But for the price, it has to be real value for money deal. ₹Pricing:- If you get this device around 60-65K, it'll be a steal deal! I've got it for 61K in the Great Indian Shopping Festival.

      • ambuj
        5 out of 5 stars
        Pretty good "Phone"
        Reviewed in India on 28 April 2022
        Verified Purchase
        Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
        Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

        This is a review for phone users, not gamers, photographers, whole-day social media people. My usage of phone is for calling, some texting, and occasional videos and photographs. My last phone lasted for more than 5 years and is still working. This is my first OnePlus phone, so I don't know about their previous phone quality.

        Look and feel:

        Feels solid in the hand, grip is good with the supplied cover.

        Battery life:

        I have been using it for over a week and for me a single charge lasts for more than a day. In fact, recently I did a drive from South India to North India of over 2000kms and the phone was connected over Android Auto for more than 10 hrs each day. The battery lasted well.

        Heating?

        I didn't find any major heating issues. Some mild heat, yes. Its similar to if you keep running any machine non-stop, or even if you keep running, your body heats up. Its normal. I am not sure what everyone's expectation is with respect to phone's not heating up. Use it reasonably, it performs very well. Well, if you are always on phone, then probably it would heat up. I don't even use 120hz refresh rate. To a normal human eye, the difference between 60-90-120hz is not perceptible. I keep it at 60, battery lasts long, doesn't heat. Phone is happy, I am happy :)

        Camera:

        Decent to nice photographs. Low ligt photography is also pretty good. For serious photography, I have a DSLR and other camera and I trust them more than any phone camera. For occasional clicks, this done a fine job.

        Gaming:

        I am not a gamer and have never played any game on any phone so don't have an opinion.

        Speed/Storage

        Ultra fast with respect to installing, uninstalling apps. 256GB storage is more than sufficient for my use. My previous phone had 64GB and in 5 years, it never got full. Well, I keep a tight control on what gets installed and downloaded on my phone. I don't let junk accumulate on phone, keeps the phone and battery life long.

        Sound:

        Very good sound quality of speakers. Well its a phone and it can do only as much. For more serious viewing, I watch on my TV and home theater.

        Overall:

        A fantastic phone at this price point. I couldn't find anything that is bad with the phone. With my usage, it will easily last for more than 4-5 years.

      • Dhruv Mepani
        5 out of 5 stars
        Best deal in the upcoming Great Indian Festival Sale
        Reviewed in India on 21 September 2022
        Verified Purchase
        Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
        Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

        I'm writing this review after using this phone for a month now and I'm glad to say that the experience is great so far.

        Firstly I'd like to inform you that I got this phone (12gb / 256gb model) for around 50k during Aug'22 sale after exchanging my old OnePlus 5T and other bank offers, so I’d like to assure that there’s no other phone in 50-55k range that comes near OnePlus 10 Pro.

        What I liked-

        • Alert Slider – I was waiting for OnePlus 10T but as soon as they announced that it won’t have Alert Slider, I switched my mind to this phone.

        • Display – This phone has the best display in the above given price range. 2k LTPO display is crisp and best for HDR / OTT viewing. Variable Refresh rate of 1-120hz is smooth & buttery when required.

        • Camera - I was not able to explore all the camera features but what I liked during my daily routine use is that it fulfills all your expectations of a perfect shot; be it normal random day-light photography, night photography, portraits, etc. This camera pack delivers quite great as its photos are as good as that of Samsung S22+ (sometimes Ultra too) & Iphone 13. What I loved most is the slo-mo video accuracy and focus.

        • UI / Software – I really liked new Oxygen OS 12 with its new features and bug-free usage.

        • Sound – Sound quality is good as it supports Dolby Atmos (headphones only) and gives out quite a bang from its 60-40 balance from bottom speaker as well as earpiece.

        What I don’t like (Scope of improvement)-

        • Switching from OnePlus 5T to this software definitely took some time to get used to but it gets better and more user-friendly with the upcoming Oxygen OS13.

        Finally, I’d like to end with a statement that during this upcoming Great Indian Festival Sale, this phone will be best in its range and no-brainer deal if you can get it between 45-50k for 128gb model & 50-55k for 256gb model after exchange & bank offers.

          Got my first One plus brand mobile after months of research to replace my 4yr old vivo v11pro. which still shines except for battery (recent months, have to charge full.. atleast 3times a day typically for my regular work).

          One plus design looks good. But will never dare to use it without case (back is too slippery) though it feels good to hold without case.

          The case given in the box is superb. matches the green colour of the phone. and of good quality

          display.. one of the very good screens i have used.

          processor... for day today tasks, there is no delay. I dont game in mobile , except for Clash of clans, so cant comment on higher end gaming.

          Phone get hot during extensive outdoor use with gps naviagation on but cools down immediatly if you give it some rest

          Same during charging. little heat can be felt.

          Battery charges in around 30mins

          Stays long for my entire days work (most of the time connected to wifi and work is indoor mostly on laptop)

          Charging brick shape is akward.. swith will automatically get pressed in most types of switchboards

          and shifting back to typa A port was bad idea. I was expecting type c to type c (even ny laptop supports type c both sides)

          and cable length is not adequate. not even full 3 feet

          Camera quality is ok. not satisfies much. will prefer dslr over this on my trips

          Night photography and video is also average. wont dissappoint (see attached video)

          Front camera needs software upgrade. not good enough ..even when compared to vivo v11pro or redmi note 10 pro max

          Overall a good overpriced phone (~50k instead of 72k). Will update review after a months use

          I waited for the 10 Pro launch and ordered on the very first day of the sale. I actually upgraded from 7T to 10 Pro – thought I would post my review based on my experience in the last few days.

          Pros:

          Look – Awesome design with a premium finish. It gives you a great feeling when you hold it.

          Charging – 80W SuperVOOC charging speeds are lightning fast. Wireless charging didn’t disappoint me either, it’s definitely a bonus.

          Camera – Amazing camera performance. With plenty of modes inbuilt, you can play if you are a camera lover. I personally liked the primary camera.

          Display – Outstanding 120Hz LTPO2 AMOLED display and great colour accuracy.

          Games – Performance is exceptionally good while playing BGMI, COD and a few other games that I play frequently.

          Cons:

          Battery – With 5000 MAH, I expected a longer battery life but it drains quicker with normal to low usage. If you are playing games, be sure to charge 2 to 3 times a day. But it's okay OnePlus got that covered with the charging speed.

          Cost – 72 k is slightly on the higher side. There are other mobiles with similar configurations which would cost about 20k-30k lesser. But with OnePlus you can always expect a 5k-10k increase in every new variant that they launch.

          If you are a OnePlus lover or want to try OnePlus for the first time and if you can afford it – simply go for it without reading any other reviews 😊..

          Rating: ⭐ (One Star is more than enough)

          I’m extremely disappointed with both the product and the post-purchase support experience.

          I purchased a phone from SA Infosys Pvt. Ltd. through Amazon, and right from day one, the device had a green line on the screen. I reached out to Amazon expecting help, but was simply told they’re just a mediator and advised to visit OnePlus customer care.

          After a quick check and a few restarts, the green line temporarily disappeared. But within days (on June 20), a pink line appeared on the display. I revisited OnePlus, and while they replaced the display after four days (June 24), they broke the back panel in the process. After raising concerns again, the back panel was eventually fixed — but from the same day, I started experiencing severe heating and battery drain issues.

          Since then, I’ve visited the service center 4–5 times, only to be told yesterday that now the motherboard is faulty.

          This has been a nightmare. I’ve spent ₹34,000 of my hard-earned money, and I’m still left without a properly functioning phone. No accountability, no permanent resolution — just frustration.

          5 out of 5 stars
          Elevating the Smartphone Experience
          Reviewed in India on 23 August 2023
          Colour: Volcanic BlackSize: 8GB RAM, 128GB Storage
          Verified Purchase
          Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
          Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

          The OnePlus 10 Pro 5G has left an indelible mark on the smartphone landscape with its exceptional features and performance. As a proud user, I can confidently say that this flagship device lives up to its hype and sets new standards for what a smartphone can achieve.

          Design Excellence:

          The OnePlus 10 Pro's design is a testament to OnePlus's commitment to aesthetics and craftsmanship. The sleek and premium build, coupled with the attention to detail, results in a device that exudes elegance from every angle. The curved glass back and metal frame not only look stunning but also feel comfortable in the hand.

          Brilliant Display:

          The display on the OnePlus 10 Pro is nothing short of breathtaking. The 120Hz Fluid AMOLED panel offers vibrant colors, deep blacks, and exceptional brightness. Whether I'm watching videos, browsing the web, or gaming, the display's fluidity and sharpness make every interaction a joy.

          Photography Mastery:

          The camera setup on the OnePlus 10 Pro is a photography enthusiast's dream come true. The Hasselblad collaboration elevates the camera performance to new heights. The versatility of the quad-camera system, along with advanced image processing, captures stunning shots in various conditions, from low light to wide-angle landscapes.

          Blazing Performance:

          Powered by the latest Snapdragon 8xx series chipset and ample RAM, the OnePlus 10 Pro delivers exceptional performance across the board. Multitasking, app launches, and even resource-intensive tasks are handled effortlessly. The device's 5G capabilities ensure fast and stable connectivity.

          OxygenOS Excellence:

          OnePlus's OxygenOS continues to be a highlight. Its clean and intuitive interface provides a smooth user experience, free from bloatware. The customization options allow users to tailor the device to their preferences, making it truly their own.

          Battery and Charging Supremacy:

          The battery life on the OnePlus 10 Pro is impressive, easily lasting through a full day of heavy use. When it's time to recharge, the Warp Charge 65T ensures lightning-fast charging, providing a substantial charge in a matter of minutes.

          5G Connectivity:

          The inclusion of 5G connectivity ensures that the OnePlus 10 Pro is future-ready. It enables seamless streaming, faster downloads, and smoother online experiences, ensuring that the device remains relevant as technology evolves.

          Final Verdict:

          The OnePlus 10 Pro 5G is a flagship device that delivers on every front. From its stunning design and brilliant display to its powerful performance and photography prowess, it stands as a true contender among the top smartphones in the market. If you're looking for a device that combines style, performance, and innovation, the OnePlus 10 Pro 5G is an absolute winner.

          Disclosure: I am a genuine user of the OnePlus 10 Pro 5G and have provided this review based on my personal experience and satisfaction with the product.

        • Abhishek vk
          4 out of 5 stars
          Loved the camera of OnePlus way beyond my expectations 👍😇👌
          Reviewed in India on 20 April 2022
          Verified Purchase
          Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
          Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

          The OnePlus 10 Pro is a great premium all-around phone - it has a good-looking screen, fast charging and powerful internals. The cherry on the cake is that it costs less than other Pro phones, making it an incredibly tempting choice. However, its Achilles’ Heel is the camera experience - there are a few problems with both the hardware and software that might put off passionate photographers.

          Additionally, the upgrades to the OnePlus 10 Pro come at nearly the same price as the OnePlus 9 Pro. However, the OnePlus 10 Pro seemed more like a solid upgrade over the 9 Pro rather than a worthy successor. I didn’t find the experience all that different. There’s definitely room for improvement in the camera department, particularly on the front. OnePlus is still playing catch-up to Samsung and Apple when it comes to camera performance and that seems to be the only thing holding it back.

          Conclusion:

          I must admit, I had low expectations for the OnePlus 10 Pro but ended up enjoying it more than the OnePlus 9 Pro. That’s primarily because I didn’t face any heating issues and the performance was tuned really well. This was a major problem with the 9 Pro last year. Plus, Oxygen OS 12 works absolutely beautifully on this phone and I am certain OnePlus will make a comeback with Oxygen OS 13, with a more streamlined design. The cameras are good enough, the display is fantastic, battery life is as good as it gets with the Snapdragon 8 Gen 1, fast charging is mad fast – what more could one really want for the price of about Rs 70,000?

          IP rating, you say? Are you hearing that OnePlus?

          Now, I wouldn’t go so far as to say that this is the comeback phone for OnePlus but it is a more refined experience compared to the OnePlus 9 Pro. That’s for sure. Which is a step in the right direction.

          What do you folks think? Let me know in the comments below.

          Bought this to run dual sim since the US version doesn't offer that. The phone itself feels no real different than my oneplus 9, though there are some weird issues, not even bugs, just design choices. Even with that turned off, data will drop for 2-3 seconds after ending a call. These things suck but I can deal with it. My real problem is the compatibility with AT&T, I use att and tello, tello uses tmobile. On my previous 2 phones (one plus 8 and 9) the att connection was much better and could use 5g. 5g does not work with att on this phone and the connection is shotty and drops if you leave the inner city. The tmobile connection works fine though. I guess I'm going to have to drop my att number and just use tmobile networks on this phone.
